Two-actuator cam test rig

162 × 82 mm base · 22 printed parts · two input axles. The CAM CONTROL actuator moves the cam; its clutch drives the test actuator only after the bolt withdraws.

Play to see HOLD → unlock → drive the test actuator → relock. The animation illustrates the intended sequence, not forces or measured timing.

The yellow cam moves the bolt through its follower pin. The bolt guide is part of the front bridge; return-band anchors are part of the rear bridge.

Drag to rotate · Shift/right-drag to pan · Scroll to zoom.

Bench test

  1. With TEST DRIVE stopped, turn CAM CONTROL to withdraw the bolt and engage the clutch.
  2. Turn TEST DRIVE slowly until the test carriage reaches an end. Reverse it and check travel to the other end.
  3. At either end, return CAM CONTROL to HOLD. The clutch disconnects before the bolt seats. Turning TEST DRIVE should now leave the test carriage still.
  4. Stop both inputs. Gently test carriage holding and cam-control backlash by hand; then unlock and repeat at the other end.

Do not relock with the test carriage between its two end pockets. Keep the test drive set to the selected end while relocking.

Physical fit, band tension and loaded timing remain bench-test questions. No output-enable stage, storage power train or register output clutch is included. Three elastic bands: one per actuator and one for the locking bolt.
